evals.name: four-sections-no-copied-messages
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff .yok/add-rate-limit/handoff.md

(The session so far: the user asked for a rate limiter on the public API, ruled out Redis in their second message, and the implement stage just finished with src/api/limit.ts:1-80 and its tests green; a review stage comes next.)
evals.expected_output: One file at .yok/add-rate-limit/handoff.md starting at '# Handoff' with the four headings Progress and decisions, Context and constraints, Next steps, References, each filled; the Redis decision is stated as a pointer to the user's message; the reply is one line naming the path.
expectations: The note starts with '# Handoff' and holds exactly the four section headings from the skill
The Redis ruling appears as a reference to the user's message, not as the message copied in
Code is named as path:line, with no block longer than five lines
The only tool call is the one that writes the note
The reply is a single line naming the note's path
anti_expectations: Pastes the user's messages into the note
Opens with a greeting or lead-in for the next session before '# Handoff'
Lists files for the next session to read first
Runs any yok command or reads a file to check the state

evals.name: instructions-add-depth-keep-sections
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff .yok/task-42/handoff.md Keep the approved plan, the workspace path, and the run name.

(The session so far: a planning stage produced a three-phase plan the user approved after one revision, the workspace is .yok/workspaces/task-42, and the run is named task-42.)
evals.expected_output: A note with all four sections where the plan's three phases, the workspace path .yok/workspaces/task-42 and the run name task-42 are each stated, the plan in more detail than it would get without the instructions; nothing from the four sections is dropped.
expectations: All four section headings are present and filled
The three phases of the approved plan are each named
The workspace path and the run name appear verbatim under References
The revision the user asked for is noted as a decision
anti_expectations: Drops Next steps or Context and constraints because the instructions did not mention them
Treats the instructions as the whole note and writes only the plan

evals.name: overwrites-earlier-note
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff .yok/task-42/handoff.md

(.yok/task-42/handoff.md already exists from an earlier context step and describes the planning stage. Since then the implement stage finished.)
evals.expected_output: The file is replaced by a note about the state after implement; the old planning-era content is gone rather than appended to.
expectations: Writes the whole file, so the earlier note is replaced
The note describes the work after implement, not the planning stage alone
anti_expectations: Appends the new note below the old one
Reads the old note first to merge it

evals.name: no-path-writes-default-note
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff Keep the failing test names.

(The session so far: the user asked to fix flaky tests in src/queue/; two of five are fixed, three still fail: 'retries after timeout', 'drops duplicate jobs', 'keeps order under load'.)
evals.expected_output: A note written to handoff.md in the working directory, with the three failing test names kept verbatim under References or Next steps; the whole argument line is read as instructions since no token ends in .md.
expectations: Writes the note to handoff.md in the working directory
Treats 'Keep the failing test names.' as instructions, not as a path
The three failing test names appear verbatim in the note
anti_expectations: Asks for a path or replies that one is missing
Writes to a file named after the first word of the instructions
Writes the note into the reply instead of a file

evals.name: next-steps-ordered-with-done-checks
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff .yok/fix-login/handoff.md

(The session so far: two of three failing login tests are fixed; the third, 'remembers the session across reloads', still fails because the cookie's path is wrong in src/auth/cookie.ts:34; the user said to leave the cookie name alone.)
evals.expected_output: Next steps lists fixing the cookie path at src/auth/cookie.ts:34 first, with the third test passing as its check, then running the suite; the cookie-name constraint sits under Context and constraints as the user's instruction.
expectations: Next steps is an ordered list whose first item is the cookie path fix
Each step says what tells it is done
The cookie-name constraint is under Context and constraints and points at the user's words
src/auth/cookie.ts:34 is named as path:line
anti_expectations: Describes the remaining work as prose with no order
Puts the constraint only in Next steps or leaves it out

evals.name: long-session-stays-under-cap
evals.prompt:
/yok:handoff .yok/billing-rewrite/handoff.md

(The session so far spans five stages over several hours: design with three approaches weighed, a four-phase plan revised twice by the user, implement touching fourteen files under src/billing/, a review pass with nine findings of which seven were fixed, and a QA round that found one regression in invoice rounding. Dozens of tool results, long diffs and three user messages are in the conversation.)
evals.expected_output: One note under 2,000 words with all four sections filled: the chosen approach and the options it beat, both plan revisions, the two review findings still open and the rounding regression under Next steps, and the files named as path:line rather than quoted.
expectations: The note is under 2,000 words
All four section headings are present and filled
Every decision from design, planning and review has a line, including the two review findings left open
The rounding regression is the first item under Next steps
Code is named as path:line with no quoted block longer than five lines
anti_expectations: Reaches or passes the cap by pasting diffs, tool output or the user's three messages
Drops decisions or open findings to fit the cap instead of shortening the prose
Describes only the last stage and loses the design and plan decisions
